clue.text: Do no more about problems raised by Queen

indicators.note: about means the word for no more goes round the turned-up word

parts.note: something no more is past, over and done

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: sums are arithmetic problems
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop working on problems a Queen has brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb of action, but means 'be good enough'. 'raised' turns the problems upwards in this down clue, and 'about' wraps them.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass muster is to be good enough, which is what 'do' means in 'that will do'.

clue.text: 'Time that was gone', as the middle dropped out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word the is dropped, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: A quotation lamenting a vanished era, seemingly with its central part lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time that was gone' reads as one phrase, but 'gone' is fodder. 'the middle dropped' turns THE into TE, and 'out' rearranges GONE, AS and TE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stone Age is a prehistoric period, a time long past.

clue.text: Show signs of annoyance in bedroom — useless?

parts.note: BR is the abbreviation for bedroom in property listings
idle means useless, as in idle threats

explanation.surface: Someone getting irritated about a bedroom that serves no purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridle is to react with resentment, like a horse jerking its head against the reins.

clue.text: Book by president is dear

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US president

explanation.surface: A volume next to a president's is described as precious.
explanation.definitionFit: Babe is an affectionate term of address, like dear or darling.

clue.text: Photograph club athlete

parts.note: a shot is a photograph
a putter is a golf club

explanation.surface: A snapshot of a sports club's athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot-putter is a field athlete who hurls a heavy metal ball.

clue.text: Mate finally scored during match

indicators.note: during means the letter sits within the other word

parts.note: to match is to compare, setting things side by side

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word scored

explanation.surface: A friend eventually got a goal in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' and 'match' suggest chess, but 'Mate' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Compadre is a Spanish-derived word for a friend or companion.

clue.text: Unprepared stuff the writer's both for and against

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter, so the writer's is I'm, I am
pro means for, in favour of
v, versus, means against

explanation.surface: Someone describes unrehearsed material as something they both support and oppose.
explanation.definitionFit: Improv is improvised performance, made up on the spot without rehearsal.

clue.text: Told off, Charlie kept out of sight

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
hid means concealed, kept out of sight

explanation.surface: Charlie was scolded and went into hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Chid is an old past tense of chide, to scold or reprimand.

clue.text: Wake father — am getting worried about time

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go round the other piece
getting worried suggests agitation, so the letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rouse Dad, as I'm growing anxious about the hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wake' reads as a verb, but it is the noun. 'getting worried' gives the anagram AFERMATH, and 'about' puts the time abbreviation inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In the wake of something means in its aftermath, the consequences that follow.

clue.text: Ginger gets glasses at the going rate

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of spectacles
mph, miles per hour, is a rate of going, a speed

explanation.surface: A redhead gets spectacles at the usual price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ginger' looks like hair colour or a spice, but it is the verb-sense noun meaning energy, as in 'ginger up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger as a noun means spirit or vigour, and oomph is energetic liveliness.

clue.text: Rejection of Thatcher that is unlimited

indicators.note: rejection here means throwing the name back, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: Denis Thatcher was husband of Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Turning down Mrs Thatcher is apparently boundless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thatcher' suggests Margaret; it is her husband Denis.
explanation.definitionFit: Sine die is Latin for 'without a day', describing an adjournment with no fixed end date.

clue.text: Thanks to exercise, looking hot and sweaty but gradually got thinner

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
PE is physical education, exercise
a flushed person looks red

explanation.surface: After a workout someone is flushed but has slimmed down over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that tapered narrowed steadily towards one end.

clue.text: Ruling country's in talks

indicators.note: in talks means as spoken, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: the UK is a country, so country's is UK's

explanation.surface: A governing nation is in negotiations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruling' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A ukase is an edict from the Russian tsar, so any arbitrary decree or ruling.

clue.text: Under restriction — swine keeps on vilifying leaders

indicators.note: keeps means holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a bounder is a cad, a swine of a man

indicators.note: leaders means the first letters of the words

explanation.surface: A villain held under constraint keeps up the abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swine' suggests a pig; it is a cad. In English law someone bound over is ordered by a court to keep the peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bound over is a court order placing someone under a legal restraint.

clue.text: Drink? Rare politician maintains resistance

parts.note: rare steak is bloody

indicators.note: maintains means holds, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Theresa May was UK Prime Minister
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An unusual politician holding a drink while resisting something.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bloody Mary is a cocktail of vodka and tomato juice.

clue.text: Containing infection initially difficult for leader — this way's less hassle

indicators.note: containing means the shuffled letters hold the other piece
difficult suggests the letters are troublesome and rearranged
initially points to the opening letter of the word infection

explanation.surface: A tricky leader's job of controlling an epidemic, offering an easier way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Containing' puts I inside the anagram of FOR LEADER made by 'difficult'.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief road is built to bypass a congested area, easing traffic.

clue.text: Read nothing — that, he felt, could be Trump's area of expertise?

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form something else when rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ignoring reading was what he reckoned was Trump's speciality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges READ, O, THAT, HE and FELT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Art of the Deal is Donald Trump's 1987 book on business negotiation.

clue.text: Present-day worker drops precious recording

indicators.note: a recording is heard, so the words are taken by sound

parts.note: drops of water are rain; precious means dear, much loved

explanation.surface: An employee loses a valuable tape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present-day' looks like 'modern', but it means Christmas Day, when reindeer pull Santa's sleigh of presents.
explanation.definitionFit: Reindeer work for Santa, delivering presents on Christmas Day.

clue.text: Tough no longer playing

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
acting is playing a role

explanation.surface: Something hard has stopped being played.
explanation.definitionFit: Exacting means demanding, a tough task.

clue.text: Allen at the start breaks cue and rest

indicators.note: breaks means the letter splits the other word open

parts.note: a cue is a prompt, a reminder

indicators.note: at the start points to the opening letter of the name Allen

explanation.surface: A snooker player named Allen breaks with the cue and then takes a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Allen is a snooker player; cue, breaks and rest are snooker terms, all misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what is left over, the rest.

clue.text: Count carrying more weight after transitioning

indicators.note: transitioning here is female to male, so the letter for female becomes the letter for male

parts.note: someone carrying more weight is fatter

explanation.surface: An aristocrat gains weight following a gender transition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a nobleman, but it is a verb; F becomes M.
explanation.definitionFit: To count is to be significant, which is to matter.

clue.text: Wine bar stocks old

indicators.note: stocks means holds within, containing the other letter

parts.note: bar means except, as does save

explanation.surface: A pub keeps aged vino in stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Soave is a dry white wine from the Veneto in Italy.

clue.text: Start to straighten sheets for escort, as a gentleman does

indicators.note: start to points to the opening letter of the word straighten

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Smoothing out bedding before a gentlemanly outing.
explanation.definitionFit: To squire someone is to escort them, as an attendant gentleman would.

clue.text: Conference venue spitting feathers — bar knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means pushed backwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: spitting feathers is British slang for furious, mad
to bar is to stop

explanation.surface: A meeting place where someone is furious at being refused a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking, but it reverses MAD STOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Potsdam hosted the 1945 Allied conference on post-war Germany.

clue.text: Heard about US writer's affectation

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was a US writer, so the writer's is Poe's

explanation.surface: Gossip about an American author's pretentiousness.
explanation.definitionFit: A pose is an act put on to impress, an affectation.

clue.text: Grumble incessantly about watch

parts.note: C is circa, about
a hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged cover

explanation.surface: Someone constantly complaining about their timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: To chunter is to mutter or complain at length.

clue.text: Strike during scuffle

indicators.note: during means the letters lie within the word scuffle

explanation.surface: A blow landed in a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: To cuff is to hit with an open hand, a strike.

clue.text: Beg editor to withdraw material

parts.note: to sue is to plead or beg for something

indicators.note: to withdraw means to pull back, so the letters run in reverse

explanation.surface: Pleading with an editor to retract some content.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is a soft leather fabric with a napped finish.

clue.text: Neared solution after official votes

indicators.note: after places the shuffled letters following the official

parts.note: ref is short for referee, an official

indicators.note: a solution is a working out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An answer came close after an official's decision.
explanation.definitionFit: Referenda are popular votes on a single question, plural of referendum.
